problems: The blind guess ('thin outline tracing the gold star-line figure', 'unrecognisable') does not name or evoke a kite with a long string and tail. The alternatives also miss it.

The kite is a thin, cramped sliver rather than a readable diamond. Apex 108036 (~147,110), top-right 107095 (~202,117), right corner 106985 (~209,168), bottom 106723 (~223,221) and lower-left 107188 (~199,210) sit so close together that the body reads as a narrow outline with no filled or recognisable kite silhouette.
The gold line work is simply traced over the stars, and the blue line is a near-duplicate offset of it. This makes it a copy of the gold lines rather than a real silhouette.
The long string has a hard right-angle bend at about (355,327), dropping straight down to the loose end 104174 at (355,470). A kite string should be a smooth, continuous trailing line.
The tail ribbon from left bridle 107556 (~177,158) out to 109139 (~84,118) is acceptable in direction, and the figure is right-way-up (apex at top, string trailing down-right).
Labels overlap and are truncated ('bottom point of the kite, wh', 'far down over t', 'loose end of the string, lef'), so the intended part of several stars cannot be read.
